newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed late, March cash soft.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed late, March cash soft.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures ended mixed Tuesday in a moderate session, with April staging a slight technical recovery, but most expected more pressure ahead with cash soft and mild weather predicted.
April climbed five cents to close at $1.865 per million British thermal units. May settled 3.3 cents higher at $1.898. Most other months ended down by one-half to 2.2 cents.

"This was a countertrend move based on oversold technicals and spreads, but the weather is going to get pretty mild and I definitely see a (upside) cap on April in the $1.95 area," said one Midwest trader.

While traders said a widening contango in the market could stir some up front buying interest and stabilize prices near here, most agreed it would take a combination of injections and cooling demand to put the market back in balance, a scenario not likely to occur before April.
Chart traders pegged April support at $1.80, then in the mid-$1.70s and then at the contract low of $1.701. Resistance was in the $1.93 area and then at $2.04.

In the cash, February Gulf Coast gas fell five to 10 cents Tuesday to the low-$1.80s, with March on the same pipes talked in the low-to-mid $1.70s. Feb Midcon gas was a few cents lower in the low-$1.70s, with March in the low-to-mid $1.60s. New York city gate gas was talked in the $2.10-2.15 area for Feb and just below $2.10 for March.
The 12-month strip rose 2.8 cents to $2.046. NYMEX said an estimated 30,343 Hub contracts traded, down sharply from Monday's revised tally of 76,466.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Tuesday.
On the KCBT, March expired seven cents higher at $1.62, while deferreds ended mixed. The East/West spread widened by 1.5 cents to 24.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
